gen-fs-quilon-gf-chocolate-classical-san: Quilon has an editorial confidence, its strokes swelling and thinning gently. Chocolate Classical Sans follows with a sizable lowercase and a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, so paragraphs of text keep an open, modern, easygoing flow.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-comme: Commanding, this heading font lets its joins slim down yet stay sturdy. Comme takes over below with a smooth, contemporary sans whose curves never clog, so a long run of text glides along without snagging.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-cossette-texte: Cossette Texte reads clean and wide-eyed, with a prominent x-height and tubelike lines. Quilon is best at gentle, editorial stroke variation up top, while the sans below does its best work as steady, unvarying text.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-duru-sans: Duru Sans keeps small letters wide open, its bodies dominating each line while ascenders barely show. Quilon above it shifts thickness softly without turning stark, and Duru Sans carries the sans-serif text beneath that display voice.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-fresca: Fresca reads modern and clean, with short ascenders above big bowls and no calligraphic thinning. Fresca's marker-like constant line is what stands apart from Quilon, whose bowls thin slightly at the sides.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-funnel-sans: Quilon's brush-like stroke shows only slight pressure variation, which gives it a commanding presence. If it were made small, though, that character would fade, while Funnel Sans keeps its tube-like constant width and pried-open e in plain sans text.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-gafata: Contemporary and professional, Gafata stacks a tall band of letters under short stalks. Quilon's modest contrast, like lightly engraved brass lettering, leads the page, and the wide-eyed sans-serif text sits beneath it.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-geist: Quilon's most distinctive trait is its modest stroke modulation, a calm editorial pulse. Geist, a plain sans with a level beat and a paper-clip opening, forms solid word blocks, and its size is where to adjust.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-georama: Georama reads approachable, with a bracelet-wide c and barely rising capitals. But if Quilon's medium-contrast strokes were made small, their editorial bite would soften, leaving the sans-serif body to carry things.
